courses.name: Linear Algebra and Ordinary Differential Equations
courses.description: Builds a firm grasp of mathematical principles through matrices, system of linear equations, eigenvalues/eigenvectors, and first/second order ordinary differential equations with engineering applications.

units.title: Matrices
units.content: Definition of matrix, Types of matrices, Algebra of matrices, adjoint, inverse of a matrix through adjoint and elementary row operations, Rank, Echelon form, Normal form, Eigen values and Eigen vectors (up to 3x3 matrices) and properties.

units.title: Applications of Matrices
units.content: Consistency of system of linear equations, Solution of system of linear equations by Gauss elimination and Gauss Jordan methods; Cayley-Hamilton theorem, Power of a matrix, Inverse of a matrix; Strength of materials and beams using eigenvalues/eigenvectors.

units.title: Ordinary Differential Equations (ODE)
units.content: First Order Differential Equations: Variable separable method, homogeneous and non-homogeneous differential equations, linear differential equations, Bernoulli equations. Second Order Linear Differential Equations with constant coefficients with RHS of form e^(ax), x^n, sin(ax) or cos(ax).

units.title: Applications of ODE
units.content: Newton’s law of cooling, Law of natural growth and decay; LR circuits.

practices: Compute inverse of a matrix if exists
Evaluate rank of matrix and prove uniqueness
Eigen values and vectors calculation
Newton's law of cooling & LR circuit modeling
skills: Find rank of matrix using different methods
Find analytical solution of differential equations
Apply numerical methods to solve differential equations

course_outcomes.outcome: Apply concepts of rank, Eigen values and Eigenvectors of a matrix and finding inverse/powers of a matrix
Apply differential equations in real life problems
Analyse the solution of a system of linear equations and find it
Inspect the analytical method for solving differential equations and applications

textbooks: B. S. Grewal, Higher Engineering Mathematics, 44th Edition, Khanna Publishers, 2018.
N. P. Bali, K. L. Sai Prasad, A Textbook of Engineering Mathematics I, II, III, 2nd Edition, 2018.
reference_books: H. K. Dass and Er. Rajanish Verma, Higher Engineering Mathematics, 3rd revised ed, S. Chand, 2015.
B. V. Ramana, Advanced Engineering Mathematics, TMH, 2011.

courses.name: Calculus
courses.description: Differential calculus, integral calculus, multivariable extreme values, double and triple integrals in polar coordinates, vector calculus, gradient, divergence, curl, and Green's/Stokes'/Gauss Divergence theorems.

units.title: Differential Calculus
units.content: Functions, Limits, Continuity, Differentiability, Tangent and normal, Mean value theorems; Extreme value and critical points, Increasing/decreasing intervals, Concavity and inflection, graphical transformation.

units.title: Integral Calculus
units.content: Double integral, Triple integral, Change of order, integration in polar coordinates, Finding Areas and Volumes.

units.title: Vector Calculus
units.content: Introduction to vectors, Vector algebra, Scalar and vector point functions, Gradient, Divergence and Curl.

units.title: Applications of Vector Calculus
units.content: Normal vector, Directional Derivative, Solenoidal and Irrotational vectors, Scalar potential; Line integral, surface integral, volume integral, Green’s theorem, Gauss divergence theorem, Stokes’ theorem.

textbooks: N. P. Bali, K. L. Sai Prasad, A Textbook of Engineering Mathematics, 2nd Edition, 2018.
B. S. Grewal, Higher Engineering Mathematics, 44th Edition, 2018.
reference_books: Erwin Kreyszig, Advanced Engineering Mathematics, 10th Edition, Wiley, 2010.

courses.name: Engineering Physics
courses.description: Quantum Mechanics, wave-particle duality, Schrödinger wave equation, 1D potential well, free electron theory of solids, semiconductor physics, Hall Effect, and optoelectronics including Lasers and Optical Fibers.

units.title: Quantum Mechanics
units.content: Wave and particle duality, de Broglie matter waves, Schrödinger’s time-independent wave equation, Eigen values/functions, 1D infinite and finite potential well, Quantum Tunnelling, Applications in SEM and Quantum dots.

units.title: Free Electron Theory
units.content: Classical and Quantum free electron theory, electrical conductivity, Fermi-Dirac distribution, electronic specific heat, Density of states, Bloch’s Theorem, Energy bands in solids.

units.title: Semiconductor Physics
units.content: Direct and indirect bandgap semiconductors, Intrinsic and extrinsic semiconductors; Carrier concentration, Fermi level, Hall Effect and temperature variation.

units.title: Optoelectronics
units.content: Photovoltaic cell, LED, LASERs (characteristics, population inversion, semiconductor diode Laser), Optical fibers (acceptance angle, numerical aperture, applications).

practices: Photoelectric Effect - Planck’s constant
I-V characteristics of p-n junction diode
Energy bandgap of p-n junction
Thermistor resistivity
Hall Effect coefficient
Laser wavelength
Optical fibre Numerical aperture
textbooks: S.M. Sze, Semiconductor Devices Physics and Technology, 3rd Ed, Wiley, 2015.
C. Kittel, Introduction to Solid State Physics, 9th Ed, Wiley, 2019.
reference_books: M. N. Avadhanulu, A Textbook of Engineering Physics, S. Chand, 2010.
